question: A 65-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of intermittent palpitations and shortness of breath. Cardiopulmonary examination shows no other abnormalities. An ECG shows an absence of P waves, an oscillating baseline, and irregular RR intervals at a rate of approximately 95 beats per minute. The difference between atrial and ventricular rates in this patient is most likely due to which of the following?

options.opa: Temporary inactivation of Na+ channels in the AV node
options.opb: Inhibition of the Na+/K+-ATPase pump in ventricular cells
options.opc: Transient activation of K+ current in Purkinje fibers
options.opd: Limited speed of conduction through the left bundle branch
options.ope: Prolonged influx through voltage-gated Ca2+ channels in the bundle of His

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Absence of P waves on ECG -> atrial depolarization not occurring -> irregular RR intervals -> atrial fibrillation -> different atrial and ventricular rates -> 95% CHAIN: Atrial fibrillation -> uncoordinated atrial contractions -> irregular ventricular response -> different atrial and ventricular rates -> 95% CHAIN: Temporary inactivation of Na+ channels in the AV node -> impaired conduction of electrical impulses from atria to ventricles -> different atrial and ventricular rates -> 95%
analysis: The ECG findings of absence of P waves, irregular RR intervals, and an oscillating baseline at a rate of approximately 95 beats per minute are indicative of atrial fibrillation. In atrial fibrillation, there is disorganized electrical activity in the atria leading to irregular impulses being conducted to the ventricles. The irregular RR intervals are a result of the varying conduction of these irregular impulses through the AV node. The absence of P waves is due to the chaotic atrial activity. Therefore, the difference between atrial and ventricular rates in this patient is most likely due to temporary inactivation of Na+ channels in the AV node.
